notes:
Summary: Pyxis is running a formal dedicated capacity eval focused on strict latency SLOs and deterministic throughput for ad-time inference. Primary ask: p50/p95/p99 definitions that match client-side timings for both streaming and non-streaming use paths.

Customer context: low-latency personalized ranking + conversational ad copy. Spikier workload w/ per-campaign bursts at top of minute. Cost sensitive but will pay for guarantees. Cannot accept public internet egress for PII — needs VPC/private control plane and KMS.

Latency SLO discussion (from calls):
- Pyxis wants p95 <= 120ms for non-streaming text-gen (single-turn responses avg 160 tokens) and p99 <= 250ms for worst-case.
- For streaming chat they expect first-byte (TTFB) p50 <= 60ms, p95 <= 150ms. Important: they measure from client send (mobile SDK) to first token streamed to client socket.
- Agreement needed on what counts as "response time": server-processing-only (edge removed), edge+network, or end-to-end client timing — they prefer end-to-end but will accept dual reporting (server-side + client-side) for contract.
- Want explicit separation of offline batching/rerank latency (can be higher) vs online scoring.

Measurement & instrumentation notes:
- Proposed approach: Redwood to provide both server-side histogram (service-level: request received -> final token emitted) and a client SDK hook that samples client-side send->first-byte/last-byte. Correlate via request-id.
- Need guidance on clock sync and skew mitigation for client-side timings; recommend using server timestamp as authoritative and report delta, plus optional NTP/SDK tagging.
- Agreed to collect p50/p95/p99 over sliding 1h windows + daily aggregates. Also want percentile windows for 5m during rollout canary.
- For streaming, measure TTFB and tail of stream gaps (median gap between streamed chunks) — Pyxis wants a max inter-chunk gap SLO (p95 <= 200ms) to preserve conversational feel.

Throughput & reserved GPU planning:
- Target baseline: 500 sustained online requests/sec (non-streaming), with burst capacity to 1.6k rps for top-of-minute campaigns. Typical payload ~ 160 tokens out / 30 tokens in.
- Initial sizing proposal: 8xA100 reserved, split into 4 pods with autoscale buffer + burst pool. Batching profile: continuous batching enabled, preferred batch size cap 32 for latency SLOs.
- Warm-up behavior: require pinned warm KV cache and pre-warmed kernels for peak campaigns; plan 10–15 minute warm-up window before major campaigns.
- Golden metrics to validate: token/sec per GPU, median kv-cache hit rate, average batch size, kernel churn events.

SLA negotiation points:
- Pyxis expects a latency-backed SLA rather than only uptime; they propose credits if server-side p95 exceeds committed SLO across monthly window. Redwood legal flagged measurement dispute resolution clause needed.
- Fallback policy: allowed automatic fallback to a slightly lower-capacity model if primary model unavailable, but must be transparent and include explicit QoS delta (e.g., expected p95 delta + quality delta).
- Data residency and audit logging add-ons to be priced separately.

POC plan & acceptance criteria:
- 4-week POC: week 1 baseline profiling (hosted), week 2 private VPC deploy + load shaping, week 3 72h soak at reserved capacity, week 4 quality/latency regressions and runbook handoff.
- Acceptance: sustained p95 <= 120ms server-side for non-streaming for 72h; streaming TTFB p95 <= 150ms; throughput validated at 500 rps with <5% error rate.

Quotes / direct customer phrasing: "We need tail latency to be predictable — spikes at campaign boundaries cannot tank our auction stack."

- Infra to provide baseline kernel/quantization plan and expected token/sec per A100 SKU.
- Legal to draft latency-SLO measurement clause and arbitration flow.
- AE to schedule procurement term-call for SLA and seat pricing (Maya).
